title: Testing Database Operations
description: Set up a test database and write async tests for CRUD operations.

slides.title: Test Database Setup
slides.content:
# Use a Separate Database

For tests, use a dedicated database (e.g., SQLite in memory) or a test database that you clean before each test.

Use `pytest` fixtures to create and tear down sessions.

slides.title: Async Test with Database
slides.content:
```python
import pytest
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, AsyncSession
from main import Base, get_db

@pytest.fixture
async def db_session():
    engine = create_async_engine("sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:")
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)
    async with AsyncSession(engine) as session:
        yield session
    # drop tables after test

# Override the get_db dependency
@pytest.fixture
def override_get_db(db_session):
    async def _get_db():
        yield db_session
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = _get_db
    yield
    app.dependency_overrides.pop(get_db, None)
```
slides.codeSnippet:
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, AsyncSession

# Simplified example
async def test_create_user(client, db_session):
    response = await client.post("/users/", json={"name": "Alice"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    # Query the test database to verify
    result = await db_session.execute(select(User).where(User.name == "Alice"))
    assert result.scalar_one().name == "Alice"

quizData.question: Why should you use a separate database for testing?

options.text: Because tests cannot run on the same database

quizData.explanation: Using a separate test database ensures tests are isolated and do not affect real data.
